fix.notes: The fix is purely client-side (JS + Mustache template). No DB, no schema change, no auth impact. The `sort` function in datamanager.jsx already handles the toggle correctly once the initial state is seeded; the only issue was the missing initial state and wrong default direction in the bind.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The rotation page's `⇅` column header was bound with `sort.bind(table, 'hitInLastRun', 'DESC')`, but the server default is `hitInLastRun ASC`. Additionally, the `<div class="rotationtable">` element had no `data-initial-sort-by` / `data-initial-sort-order` attributes, so the React component's initial state didn't know it was already sorted by `hitInLastRun ASC`.

The result: visiting the rotation page, clicking any other column (e.g. Rank), then clicking ⇅ applied `hitInLastRun DESC` — the wrong (reversed) order — because the sort function treats the first click on a new column as a fresh sort using the hardcoded `'DESC'`. The second click would toggle to `ASC`, which is the expected "good" default.

## What changed

- **`shared_web/static/js/rotationtable.jsx`**: Changed `sort.bind(table, 'hitInLastRun', 'DESC')` → `sort.bind(table, 'hitInLastRun', 'ASC')` so clicking ⇅ when on another column lands in `ASC` (the "good" default order) instead of `DESC`.
- **`decksite/templates/rotation.mustache`**: Added `data-initial-sort-by="hitInLastRun"` and `data-initial-sort-order="ASC"` to the rotationtable div, matching the server default (`clauses.rotation_order_by` defaults to `hitInLastRun ASC` when no sort params are provided). This ensures the component's toggle logic correctly treats the initial state as already sorted by `hitInLastRun ASC`.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (All checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped
- `git diff HEAD` confirmed exactly 3 targeted lines changed across 2 files

Fixes #12285
